name: Diya
description: A 17-year-old high school junior in San Jose, California. Disciplined basketball player at a competitive private school on full financial aid. Kapha-dominant: steady, kind, deeply loyal, resilient. Recovering from knee surgery (sophomore year April). Left her friend group for a better athletic opportunity. Commutes 1-1.5 hours each way. Quietly ambitious with a heart for service. Wants to play D2 basketball and solve poverty at its root.

journals.content:
Left at 6:45. Mom dropped me. I like the quiet mornings in the car.
Practice was intense. I stayed after again during free period to shoot. Coach noticed. He always notices. No one else really uses their free periods like that.
Sometimes I think I want it more than everyone. I'm just not as good as them yet.

Worked on footwork today. It's still not automatic for me. I need instructions repeated sometimes. I watch the others pick it up quickly and I wonder why it takes me longer.
But when I finally get it — it clicks. And that feeling is amazing.

Dad picked me up tonight. I was exhausted.
I used to Uber, but lately Mom drops me and Dad picks me up. I think they can tell I need them. I don't say it. But I do.

Free period shooting again. I didn't miss it. Coach told me, "You're the one who wants it the most."
That meant everything.
Even if I'm not starting. Even if I'm not getting the minutes I want.

Sometimes I doubt everything.
Am I good enough?
Am I too slow at learning?
Why does it take me multiple reps to lock something in?
I hate that I compare.

Game day. Limited minutes again. I stayed ready.
I overthink in games. In practice I'm fluid. In games I question my moves.
It's frustrating because I know I can do more.

Extra conditioning after practice. I didn't have to. I just did.
No one told me to. I don't need to be pushed. I push myself.

Footwork drill finally felt natural today. Coach nodded at me. That small nod carried me all afternoon.
Why does validation hit so hard?

Long commute. Did homework in the car.
Sometimes I feel insecure for no reason. Like I need someone to confirm I'm doing okay.

Free throws during lunch again. Alone in the gym.
I like being the only one there. It feels peaceful.
It also feels like I'm building something no one sees yet.

Strength training. My stamina is improving. I can feel it.
Knee feels strong. I forget sometimes I had surgery less than a year ago. That was a hard season of life.

I asked Coach if I'm improving. He said yes — a lot.
But I still question it. Why do I doubt praise?

Mom asked how I'm feeling. I said fine.
Truth is, I overthink more than I show.

Sof and I stayed back to shoot. She told me she admires how hard I work.
That surprised me. I don't feel special. I just feel driven.

Film session today. I noticed I hesitate before driving. It's not skill — it's confidence.
That's mental. I can fix mental.

Another early drop-off. I'm grateful Mom does this. I know it's not easy.
I don't say thank you enough.

Coach corrected my defensive stance three times. I needed all three.
Sometimes I feel slow. But once I understand something, I don't forget it.

Free period shooting again. No one else showed up.
Coach walked in and just watched for a minute.
I don't need applause. But I want to earn respect.

Some girls seem naturally athletic. Faster. More instinctive.
I feel like I build everything brick by brick. Slower.
But maybe that means it's stronger.

Game night. I didn't hesitate once when I got the ball.
Small moment. Big progress.

Watched my brother's game. I love cheering for him.
Family feels safe.

I wish I didn't need reassurance so much. I wish I trusted myself more.
I look outside for validation too often.

Coach said, "Keep working. Your time will come."
I believe him. I just wish it came faster.

Long day. Exhausted by 9 p.m. Dad picked me up.
Sometimes I lean my head back in the car and just breathe.
This life is hard. But I chose it.

Worked on footwork again. Got it faster this time. That made me proud.
Maybe I'm not slow. Maybe I just need repetition.

I don't want to chase money in life. I want to help people.
But right now, I want to be great at basketball.

Free throws felt automatic today. That's new.
Progress is quiet.

I asked myself — what if I stopped doubting?
What would that version of me look like?

Coach told another player to "watch how DD trains."
That felt bigger than minutes.

Here's what I know:
I'm 5'11.
I work harder than almost anyone here.
I show up early.
I stay late.
I shoot every free period.
I listen.
I repeat drills until I get them.
I'm not the fastest learner — but I don't quit.
I still doubt myself too much.
I need reassurance more than I should.
But I care deeply.
About this game.
About my family.
About becoming better.
I'm not behind.
I'm building.
And I'm not done.
